page: Microsoft Azure E96-24s_v5 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the ESv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz, configured with 12 physical cores and 24 virtual cores (vCPUs) with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with an exceptionally large memory capacity of 672.0 GB, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 28.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable for remote disk attachments.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong memory performance, with a Passmark memory score in the top 25% and a large-block memory write bandwidth of 106.74 GB/sec, also in the top 25%. CPU performance is solid, with a Passmark CPU score of 30,451.25 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 23,302.98, both falling within the average range. For database and memory-bound operations, the system achieved 23.93 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks and a static web serving throughput of 28.2 GB/sec.

The E96-24s_v5 is designed for memory-intensive workloads that do not require a proportional scaling of compute resources. By constraining the active vCPUs to 24 while maintaining a 672.0 GB memory footprint, this server offers high qualitative cost efficiency for database engines and enterprise applications licensed on a per-core basis. It is highly suited for large relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, data analytics, and memory-heavy enterprise workloads.
